id_and_class.summary: Leslie Dewart holds that all animals experience but only humans experience consciously, and that speech, not genetic natural selection, produced this difference. Assertive speech, in which a speaker intends to communicate her experience and undergoes the communicating as her own doing, makes experience present to itself: the subject experiences the object, the act of experiencing, and herself as experiencer in one act. Consciousness then develops culturally and historically, and it can develop badly.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Self-Present Experience Generated by Speech

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is self-present experience, in which the act of experiencing is present to itself without any separate act of reflection, made possible by assertive speech.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Consciousness is fully natural and caused by the same biochemical processes humans share with animals, but it is a new way of using those processes and does not reduce to them.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Cultural-historical emergence: consciousness arises from a mode of action (speaking) rather than from a new biological structure, and keeps evolving through culture.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: In conscious experience the subject is given to herself in the very act of experiencing, prior to any self-observation, which Dewart offers as a way around Henrich’s circularity objection to reflection theories of self-consciousness.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Dewart grants experience to animals and reserves ‘consciousness’ for its self-present human form, so he explains how experience becomes present to itself but not why any state feels like anything.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Animal organisms and their biochemical processes, experience, assertive speech, and culture as an inheritance mechanism.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through phenomenological description of self-presence, combined with evolutionary, linguistic, and historical analysis.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: One act with three moments: encountering reality, experiencing one’s own experiencing, and experiencing oneself as experiencer.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-conscious (self-present) human experience, thought, and cultural development of mind; not basic sentience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Assertiveness: unlike animal signaling, human speech asserts a thesis about a theme and is experienced by the speaker as her own causal act, which makes experience present to itself.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Speech comes first, consciousness second, and structured languages third, a sequence Dewart holds every child recapitulates. Internalized speech becomes thought, and consciousness continues to evolve culturally.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Uniquely human in the 1989 account, though Pikkarainen notes Dewart softened the denial of animal consciousness in his posthumous work.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness opens existential questions and drives cultural evolution. When it develops only partially (‘absent-mindedness’), the subject projects her own asserting outward and feels reality speaking to her, which Dewart takes as the origin of the sacred.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Dewart rejects ‘representationism’, the doctrine that cognitions are copies of their objects in the mind, which he traced to Hellenistic sources.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Speech started a new evolutionary process alongside genetic evolution: culture, rather than natural selection, now carries and transforms consciousness.
core_claims_and_evidence: All animals experience, but only humans experience consciously, in the sense of self-present experience.
The manner of speaking formats consciousness, which then shapes languages, so grammar does not condition thought.
Indo-European and Sumerian copular sentences (‘X is Y’) encode a reality insisting on itself, a contested claim Dewart uses to diagnose absent-mindedness.
Genuine thought and speech require a self-oriented purposive process, so computers can only simulate them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and phenomenological, supported by evolutionary, developmental, and comparative linguistic arguments.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The linguistic claim about copulas is contested, and the assumption that purposiveness is possible only in living organisms is asserted rather than argued. The stark denial of animal consciousness in the 1989 book sits uneasily with granting animals experience.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Explaining how experience becomes self-present does not explain why experience is phenomenal at all, a question Dewart leaves on the animal side of his boundary. The work has received little attention in mainstream consciousness research.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a non-reductive naturalism that keeps consciousness natural without reducing it to neural activity, though its cultural-historical claims extend well beyond what the ontology requires.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Dewart argued that genuine thought and speech require the system to communicate its contents to itself as a self-oriented purposive process, which he held only living organisms can do.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since consciousness here is a natural use of an organism’s biochemical processes, the view gives no basis for it continuing after death.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Dewart traces the sense of a Power speaking through the world to a partial development of consciousness that projects human agency outward.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A digital system would on his view only simulate speech and thought, lacking the self-presence of a living speaker.
